svg.title: compose-add-comment · long · 160x48
svg.text: +Run `viewer FILE`, then press `j` and `k` to move.
more detail. Here's what I'd add:
- `j` / `k` move one line and stop at either end of the file; they
- `G` jumps to the last line and `g` to the first.
- `J` / `K` move by hunk, and stop at the first and the last hunk.
- The arrow keys do the same as `j` and `k`, and page up and page down
I checked each of these against the current build and they all behave
as described, so this is only a docs change. If you want, I can open a
follow-up for wrapping around at the ends, but I'd keep it behind a
setting so the default stays the same as today.
The help panel lists `j` as "Line down" but the footer says "Down". We
should pick one; I'd go with the help panel's wording because it's
1. Open a file longer than the screen
4. Press `J` and `K` on a file with three hunks
Every one of them stopped where the docs will say it stops. The only
surprise was `K` on the first hunk, which does nothing rather than
wrapping to the last one, and that matches the rest.
The screenshot in the README is from 0.5 and still shows the old title
bar. It'd be worth refreshing it in the same PR.
A few notes for whoever picks up the wrap-around follow-up:
- keep the default as it is today
- put the setting next to the other viewer settings
- make `G` and `g` respect it too, so the keys stay consistent
That's all from me on this line.
